### How this work is cited

Passages inside Guide of the Perplexed are identified by part, chapter (e.g. iii.51). Written in Judeo-Arabic for a student, and Maimonides states in the introduction that he has deliberately scattered his argument and withheld conclusions that could be misread. That warning is part of the text: a single chapter quoted alone is the reading he asked against.

### The work in Maimonides’s thought

Moses ben Maimon (1138–1204), known as Maimonides or Rambam, fled Almohad persecution from Córdoba to Fez and finally to Egypt, where he served as a communal leader and court physician. He codified Jewish law in the Mishneh Torah and wrote the Guide of the Perplexed for readers torn between Torah and Aristotelian science. [More on Maimonides](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/maimonides) .
